subject: Sequencing playbook: evaluation MAP, acceptance gates & MSA/DPA order form timing
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@nimbushealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP + eval plan + target close window

Monica —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to capture a pragmatic MAP and a deliverable-level evaluation plan so they can line up their legal review and budget committee. Our target is a production contract signed before the end of Q4; procurement prefers a concrete gating checklist they can map to their internal milestones.

High level ask: can you share a MAP with:
- evaluation milestones (tech POC, security review, legal review) with owner and estimated days-to-complete
- the minimal MSA/DPA redlines that would trigger longer legal review (we're flexible on price/term negotiation but need clarity on data residency & audit clauses)
- a working assumption for when an order form can be signed (after DPA or in parallel?)

If you can attach a working MAP spreadsheet, procurement will overlay their calendar and get back with required procurement gating dates.

Thanks — I copied procurement so they have visibility.

Alyssa
Director, Cloud Integrations
Nimbus Health

Attachment: none (procurement asked us to get your MAP in spreadsheet form)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: RE: MAP + eval plan + target close window

Alyssa —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a first-pass MAP spreadsheet (Nimbus_MAP_v1.xlsx) and a short narrative below that maps our typical sequencing and options for parallelization. Please review and tell me which procurement milestone (e.g., budget committee, security attest) is the real blocker on your side and we’ll tighten dates against that.

Key proposal (summary):
1) Technical POC (2 weeks) — Redwood engineering + Nimbus infra lead. Goal: validate API, end-to-end latency at target workloads.
2) Security questionnaire / evidence (SOC2 report, dataflow diagram) — parallel to POC; expected 3–5 business days to deliver standard artifacts.
3) DPA review (legal) — two tracks:
   - If Nimbus can accept our standard DPA -> sign within 5 business days after review.
   - If redlines requested that touch data residency/audit/KMS, allow 10–15 business days for legal negotiation.
4) MSA (commercial) — majority of price/term negotiation can happen in parallel to DPA; MSA signature can be completed before or at the same time as the order form depending on your procurement rules.
5) Order form — we recommend drafting the order form early (we included an OrderForm_Draft.pdf) and using a placeholder effective date; final signature ideally within 3 business days of MSA+DPA alignment.

Three sequencing options (spreadsheet has the gating columns):
- Fast-path: run POC + security in parallel, accept standard DPA, sign MSA and Order Form within 3–5 business days once legal confirms no residency redlines. (target: 3 weeks)
- Standard path: POC -> legal review (DPA) -> MSA -> Order Form (target: 6–8 weeks)
- Conserved path: if DPA redlines are significant, plan for an extended legal window and MSA hold; we’ll plan milestone-based pilot billing until final order form is signed.

Action items for Nimbus (please reply):
- Which path do you want to target? (Fast / Standard / Conserved)
- Who on procurement will own the signature deadline?
- Any must-have DPA clauses to flag now (residency, audit frequency, vendor subprocessor list)?

I’m happy to run a short align call with your procurement and legal this week to walk the MAP. Karthik — I’ve copied you for legal take and any required redline guidance we should include in the spreadsheet.

Best,
Monica Patel
Program Lead, Enterprise GTM
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Nimbus_MAP_v1.xlsx; OrderForm_Draft.pdf

Forwarding my notes back to the thread — short legal POV and recommended timeline language to put into the MAP.

----- Forwarded message -----
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-28T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Legal gating notes (summary)
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Monica / team —

High level legal comments for Nimbus MAP: 
- Standard DPA acceptance is the quickest path. If they propose residency or HSM-specific KMS requirements we should:
  a) propose an alternative scope that limits residency to log storage only and keep model inference ephemeral; or
  b) offer a Private deployment quote (longer procurement) if residency can’t be relaxed.
- Redlines likely to extend DPA by 7–12 business days depending on scope. Communicate this as a contingency in the MAP.
- MSA commercial redlines (warranty, indemnity caps) typically do not block signature if we place them in a negotiation appendix and allow Order Form to proceed with a placeholder reference. Recommend contractual language to permit pilot usage under a signed quote with final MSA to follow within 30 days.

Suggested MAP gating language to add to spreadsheet: 
- "DPA accepted (standard) -> legal signoff (5bd)"
- "DPA material redlines -> legal review window (7–12bd)"
- "Order form can be countersigned and executed with a placeholder effective date if both parties agree in writing; final MSA to be executed within 30 days"

I will attach a redline summary (MSA_redlines_v2.docx) for your internal review. If procurement at Nimbus insists on order-of-operations, advise they allow Order Form signature to proceed in parallel to commercial MSA negotiation to avoid losing quarter-close.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@nimbushealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@nimbushealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sequencing playbook: evaluation MAP, acceptance gates & MSA/DPA order form timing

Monica / Karthik —

This is very helpful — procurement reviewed the MAP and we want to pursue the Fast-path with one caveat: their calendar requires an Order Form signed by 2026-10-22 to hit the committee that week. Procurement also flagged two must-have commitments in the DPA: (1) a clear audit schedule for access logs and (2) confirmation of encryption-at-rest controls + KMS controls.

Next steps from our side: procurement will try to accept Redwood's standard DPA; if they submit redlines that touch residency we’ll let you know immediately. Procurement also asked us to accept the pilot-as-placeholder approach you suggested so the order form can lock pricing and scope while legal completes final MSA.

Our asks for Redwood:
- Can we get a signed Order Form (placeholder effective date) by 2026-10-20 so procurement can circulate to the committee?
- Karthik — can you confirm that the two DPA items above can be represented in our standard DPA and provide the SOC2 artifact and a dataflow diagram (Grace, can you help with the diagram?)

We can do a short call Friday (2026-10-02) 10:00–10:30 PT if that helps.

Alyssa
Director, Cloud Integrations
Nimbus Health
